items.definition: Architecture Decision Record: one decision, why, and what follows. An accepted ADR outranks code and chat.
One physical garment with its own barcode.
A checked copy of the encrypted database kept in two places (a USB drive and a folder); the last 60 are kept in each.
Percentage as an integer; 100 basis points = 1% (5% is 500). Used so percentages never need a float
One purchase receipt (GRN) with a code of YYMM plus a 3-digit lot.
Looks like 2026-27/C1/000123: financial year (April to March), counter, and that counter's running number. Two counters never clash.
Cash close where the cashier enters denominations and does not see the expected amount.
One billing station with its own local database and counter ID.
Barcode voucher issued on a return, with an expiry date.
Ledger of all money movements.
Goods received note: entry of new stock.
The sticker or tag on a garment showing shop name, style, size, color, MRP and the barcode
A 3-digit number in the barcode; each counter owns a range of lots so counters never issue the same barcode
Counter app mode for the owner, with cost data and reports.
A price reduction below MRP set by the owner, as a percentage or a fixed amount. A marked-down garment takes no cashier discount
Maximum retail price printed on the hangtag.
Integer money unit; 100 paise is 1 rupee.
The single table in `core_domain` of which role may do which action; anything not listed is denied
The database key written as groups of hex digits and shown once to the owner. With a backup it opens the data on a new computer.
Days after a sale a cashier may take a return alone (7); later needs a manager or owner.
Counter app mode for the cashier, with no cost data.
Block of barcode serials reserved for one counter.
Period a cashier works between opening and blind close.
A product in one size and color with its price.
